title: OpenAI invoke: stream consistency and tool-schema bridge
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: In production we observed two classes of failures when using the OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling: 1) streaming fragmentation could cause transient, inconsistent 'tool_choice' decisions when partial fragments arrived at the runtime, and 2) heterogeneous tool schemas (legacy function defs from older integrations) created noisy mappings that increased false positives for tool selection and made deterministic repros difficult. This PR introduces a compatibility bridge and a deterministic path to stabilize tool selection during streaming and to normalize tool/function schemas for downstream consumers.

What this change does (summary): canonicalizes tool schemas at ingress, introduces a compact tool_choice_v2 envelope with deterministic tie-break semantics, and adds a streaming coalescer that protects the tool selection decision from transient fragment reorder/partial updates. The compatibility bridge performs non-destructive mapping from legacy function signatures to the canonical runtime shape; mappings are recorded as schema provenance metadata that flows with the request for auditability.

Key user-visible behavior: clients using the OpenAI-compatible /v1/ functions/tool-call surface should see no breaking changes. On the server side, tool invocations are more stable during streaming: we avoid flip-flopping tool choices mid-response, and we attach provenance and schema_hash metadata to each resolved invocation. Feature rollout is behind the openai.invoke_compat_v2 feature flag.

Implementation notes: the PR touches three logical areas: api/openai_adapter (compat bridge and normalizer), serving/stream (coalescing and boundary markers), and serving/dispatch (deterministic tool_choice resolver). The resolver uses a deterministic ranking key composed of (rank_score, schema_hash, provenance_age, deterministic_fallback_counter) to ensure always-reproducible selection across replays. The streaming coalescer implements a short (configurable) stabilization window for tool choice decisions that merges adjacent fragments unless a final 'invoke_commit' marker is received. This keeps latency impact minimal while preventing false mid-stream choice flips.

Testing and telemetry: added unit tests for the normalizer, fuzz tests that validate deterministic resolver properties, and integration tests that exercise fragmented-stream scenarios with reorder and partial frames. Benchmarks show the stabilization window introduces ~1.1ms median added latency in the worst-case path and reduces choice flip rate by ~98% on our canary workload. New telemetry events (tool.choice_resolved, tool.schema_mapped, tool.choice_stabilized) are emitted to assist rollout monitoring.

Migration notes: platform teams do not need to change function definitions, but large integrators that previously relied on ad-hoc parameter shapes should validate the canonical mapping. The compatibility bridge logs any lossy mappings to the audit log and surfaces suggested schema fixes in the Console guidance panel.

Related tasks: ENG-4312 (compat bridge), ENG-4400 (stream coalescer), PM-217 (rollout plan), SRE-98 (canary and alerting).
commits: init: add openai compat v2 adapter and schema registry
serving(stream): implement fragment coalescer and boundary markers
dispatch: deterministic tool_choice resolver and provenance scoring
api: canonical schema normalizer + legacy mapping table
tests: add fuzz/integration tests for fragmented invoke paths
docs: add openai compatibility migration guide and telemetry notes
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Requested changes - please add a regression test for the case where two tools have identical rank_score but different schema_hash to ensure deterministic fallback ordering.
Maya Chen: Added tie-break unit test and updated tool_choice.go to prefer schema_hash before provenance_age; pushed fix.
Arjun Rao: Noted potential N+1 on schema registry lookups during bursty traffic. Suggest caching at request-scoped level.
Maya Chen: Implemented request-scoped cache with TTL and added a microbenchmark; see commit 'api: add request cache for schema registry'.
Sofia Patel: Approved after CI green and two approvals. Noted that SRE should watch tool.choice_stabilized alerts during rollout.
merge_details: Squash and merge by Sofia Patel after 2 approvals and green CI. Rollout gated by feature flag 'openai.invoke_compat_v2' with canary percentage 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
release_notes: Improves stability of OpenAI-compatible function/tool invocations during streaming. Adds a canonical schema mapping layer and deterministic tool_choice resolution to prevent mid-stream flips. No breaking changes to the public /v1/ function/tool-call API. Operators: enable 'openai.invoke_compat_v2' feature flag and monitor 'tool.choice_stabilized' telemetry. See docs/openai_compat_migration.md for mapping guidance.
notes_on_performance: Canary microbenchmarks: median latency +1.1ms for stabilization window worst-case, 98% reduction in tool_choice flip-rate; CPU and memory impact within acceptable SLOs. Added bench comparisons in docs/benchmarks/openai_invoke_stability.md.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for normalizer and resolver (coverage +7%), fuzz test found and fixed a reorder bug, integration tests simulate fragmented streams and validate no mid-stream tool flips. CI flake: one intermittent e2e timeout was rerun and passed.
